claims.claim: Players report that the game features a modding community that adds extra content and campaigns like the Downfall expansion.

citations.review_text:
Watch friend playing it, then decide to buy it. And now I understand why he's addicted to this game.
Also the modding community on this game is absolutely incredible.

Excellently Balanced and gets quite challenging at higher ascensions especially at Ascension 20. Beating Act4 on there is no joke. Missing some QoL which can be added back in with mods.
Speaking of mods, it really feels infinitely moddable with the amount of additional content that can be added to it. Downfall expansion mod basically adds a whole new separate campaign on top of the base game.

In comparison to the second game wise, Ironclad's and Defect's kits feels similar but still distinctly different, silent is comparable between the two games although game context makes it feel different. Watcher, Necrobinder and Regent are completely different experiences altogether. 
The only thing really feeling missed in the first game is the multiplayer aspect of the second, but even then there are mods which can achieve similar thing.

All that being said, STS1 and STS2 are both excellent games which i've put hundreds of hours combined and would reccomend getting both if able to experience the difference in design philosophy between the two games

single_points.text: One reviewer says the music is the same the whole game and they should have added a more varied soundtrack considering how much the game is replayed.

citation.review_text:
[h1]Maten a la aguja (?[/h1]

1) Es [b]ALTA[/b]mente rejugable… Es divertidísimo y, por bastante tiempo, sentis que cada run tiene cosas nuevas 💯
2) Los eventos random están buenisimos, son variados y te dan casi siempre varias opciones entre las que elegir 👍
3) Está bueno que los textos tengan efectos. Por ejemplo, las letras vibran, tienen distintos colores, etc 🔊
4) Tiene un buen nivel de dificultad. Se siente [i]desafiante[/i], pero ni por cerca imposible.
5) Muy Buena variedad de cartas, relics, etc. Hay muchísimas 🔥
6) 100 playtesters, y ¿ninguno te dijo que pongas un boton para "volver atras" si le pifiaste de carta? No creo que sea algo que te rompa el juego, y no viene mal que esté 🫠 [strike]en realidad me quejo por que soy manco[/strike]
7) El vendedor tendría que darte opciones para [b]curarte[/b] 🩹 por un cierto precio, y también para que puedas [b]vender[/b] objetos 💸 
8) La musica está buena, pero es la misma [u]tooodo[/u] el jueguito y la idea es que lo rejuegues 10000 veces... Por esa razón, para mi tendrían que haberle metido más pilas a un soundtrack más variado 🎶🎵

En resumen: ¿para qué lees mi reseña si el jueguito ya tiene "Overwhelmingly Positive"?
[i]Es un juegazo men.[/i]

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as very difficult, particularly at higher ascension levels or when attempting to master it.

citations.review_text: What a game. One of the only true representations of adaptability in gaming history, a game with amazing combat system that forces you to adapt throughout the whole gameplay, but aesthetically not all that pleasing, and it has pretty mid music, tho it's still enjoyable, and it fits the game. The Characters are very interesting and they each have there own mechanics, while also having a large pool of incredible items, relics, and cards. One of the hardest 100% ever, could be debatable for THE hardest, truly an astonishingly tough game to master. 9/10

writing this after getting 100% completion and I must say it's one of if not the best card game(if you don't hate rougelikes).
it has a lot of difficulty levels I only beat the hardest one with one of the 4 characters(poison deck) and to make your life harder even a secret boss.

On sale it's really worth it even if you haven't touched deck builders yet. Not a must buy, more like a nice expirience even if you won't play for long I guess.

Northerlion once said, "Slay the Spire is worth about $2,400 as a game", and while that might be a bit of a stretch, it's somewhat true. This game is fun, addicting, frustrating, and devastating, all at once. It's the perfect combination of classic TCGs like Magic: The Gathering, YuGiOh!, and Hearthstone, mixed together with the roguelike elements that make games like Risk of Rain 2 and Hades so great. I don't think I've ever played a game where losing makes you want to instantly try again as much as this game does. Every heartbreaking defeat in this game is made up for by the impossible victories, pulled back straight from the jaws of certain death. 

I have almost 180 hours in Slay the Spire, have beaten the heart on A1 with 3/4 characters, and have beaten A20 as the Ironclad. With that being said, I think I have experienced just about everything that this game has to offer at this point, aside from beating the heart with the Watcher, and doing A20 climbs on other characters. Also, I haven't done the heart on A20, but... yeah, no thanks. Beating the Heart and conquering the A20 climb are both incredibly monumental tasks and I applied anyone who has the patience to do them, especially A20. It is NOT easy, and will take a lot of time, effort, and practice before you get there. Less than 8% of players have actually ever beaten A20, so it's easy to forget that doing so is something that the vast majority of players will never actually accomplish, either because they aren't skilled enough, or, because they just don't have the time, patience, or interest in beating the game 20 times in a row like an actual fiend. 

For such a simple game, there is a lot of strategy involved, and when you really start to learn the nuances of deckbuilding, pathing, and how to weigh risk vs reward, the doors of this game start to open up to you. There is a lot of luck involved in this game for sure, but, you "make your own luck", as they say. I absolutely 100% recommend this game. I won't …

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple distinct characters, each with their own mechanics and play styles.

citations.review_text: What a game. One of the only true representations of adaptability in gaming history, a game with amazing combat system that forces you to adapt throughout the whole gameplay, but aesthetically not all that pleasing, and it has pretty mid music, tho it's still enjoyable, and it fits the game. The Characters are very interesting and they each have there own mechanics, while also having a large pool of incredible items, relics, and cards. One of the hardest 100% ever, could be debatable for THE hardest, truly an astonishingly tough game to master. 9/10

As someone who does not usually play card games this is the one anyone similar to me makes an exception to

It simply one of the best balanced and fun rougue likes I played, its very hard but has a modular difficulty system with 20 progressing harder difficulties, so as you master a character you will keep being challenged

All characters have their own unique gimmicks and decks, and you clearly see archetypes and combos within the available cards, which both hint at their abilities and personality

Using said combos and hunting for those combinations, together with your relics and passives to make your deck greater than the sum of its parts changes how you see many of the items and cards depending on your circumstances, so every card and item has its place and situation where it truly shines

The enemies are also one of the high points of the game, the bosses and mini bosses all demand different deck styles and damage/blocking solutions, so you are pushed into specialising your deck or covering your weakness depending on what comes next, with the true final boss being the best designed boss I ever saw, demanding that your deck is fully fleshed out, consistent and capable of doing massive damage and great block

In all its a great game that even people that dont like deckbuilders will love it

This is a great and frustrating deck builder card game. You get 4 play styles to try out and really they are so different its crazy. N 2 games will be alike, as you will get new perks in the form of totems, cards, and random encounters. Some runs will be so amazing you will feel like you built the perfect deck but then you happen to run into a basic enemy and the RNG of cards and the RNG of their attacks means sometimes you will always draw attacks when you seriously need to defend and defense cards when they are not attacking. plus some times they pull off a 4 solid attacks of your full life total in a row and if you somehow can defend each one they magically have another massive attack regardless how your deck is built. Still alot of fun plus mods make it so you pretty much have endless options for variation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game offers high replayability due to randomized elements and varying run combinations.

citations.review_text:
Slay the Spire looks simple at first, yet there's so much depth once you start experimenting with different strategies. It is incredibly satisfying to put together a deck that somehow works perfectly and watching your enemies get absolutely destroyed.

For me, it's also one of those games I can just sit back and relax with. If a run falls apart, I just feel like trying a new run again and see what I could've done differently.

There are countless of combinations to try which makes for an incredible amount of replayability. I highly recommend this game.

Hands down the best roguelike deck builder out there.Extremely addicting and literally every run is different due to the random events and cards,forcing you to adapt your build each time.It gives you massive highs where you get your synergies going and become unstoppable,and really low lows where you get destroyed cause the deck just doesn't work.Also there has never been a time where I felt this much adrenaline in a game as when I was trying to beat Ascension 20.

Its fantastic. I have way more hours offline because I play it when away from home a lot. Surprisingly simple to grasp but incredibly deep once you start to learn it. Randomisation of each run means nothing can be predicted and makes success even better. I waited to get all achievements before buying Slay the Spire 2.

I play this game WAAAAY more than I probably should. It's such a pure and wholesome experience. Not because the subject matter is wholesome or because the story deals with uncomplicated topics. No, the reason this game is "wholesome" and "pure" is because the game is as simple as simple gets. Slay the Spire is a game that features window dressing around very simple and easy to understand game mechanics. Sometimes, that simplicity is the best thing a gamer can ask for.

Slay the Spire kind of has a story, but it's one that's not really told as more so inferred. You play as one of three (later 4) different warriors summoned to a massive spire by an ancient god. Why these warriors have answered this call and what they hope to gain from the journey is vague at best, but nevertheless have all agreed to attempt to conquer the spire. You must ascend to the top of the spire, choosing a path that best suits your needs, facing randomly generated threats as you go.

The story's lore is inferred through the game's simple but efficient artstyle and rigged-based and extremely limited animation. You can also find crumbs of lore and backstory in card art, some interactions in the game and certain choices made in certain segments. Slay the Spire is a dark, otherworldy, Lovecraft-meets-Hieronymus-Bosch world that features ancient gods and monsters that want to devour your flesh or suck out your soul. But there's no real narrative or a plot to follow beyond go to the top of the tower and kill the monsters. The Spire seems to have a civilization inside of it, the monsters seemed to be connected the treasures you find, the boss's seemed to have history outside of the spire, and yet none of it really makes a difference to your expeirence. This is not a story-driven game; the setting is an encouraging carrot on the stick to compel us to play.
